prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 会议室预订周视图（5/12–5/16） (language zh-CN).
Grid: 6 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "2025 春季校园招聘宣讲会（09:00–17:" spans 3 col × 1 row; "产品需求评审（09:00–12:00）｜A301" spans 1 col × 2 row; "新员工入职培训（13:30–16:30）｜C20" spans 1 col × 2 row; "客户方案演示与答疑（13:30–16:30）｜A" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "时间段" · longest unbreakable word 53px · one-line width 94px
  col 2: header "周一（5/12）" · longest unbreakable word 65px · one-line width 261px
  col 3: header "周二（5/13）" · longest unbreakable word 65px · one-line width 214px
  col 4: header "周三（5/14）" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 274px
  col 5: header "周四（5/15）" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 304px
  col 6: header "周五（5/16）" · longest unbreakable word 62px · one-line width 190px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 682px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 681px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A weekly room-booking grid: a reader either (a) runs down one weekday column to find a free slot, or (b) reads across one time band to compare which day/room is free — it is a lookup-and-compare table, not a reading table, so the time axis and the day columns must be scannable at a glance rather than prose-legible.","reading":"Top-left time label → down the column for the target day, or across the row for the target slot. Merged blocks (Mon 产品需求评审, Wed 新员工入职培训, Thu 客户方案演示 spanning 09:00–10:30+10:30–12:00 / 13:30–15:00+15:00–16:30, and the 3-column 全天 banner over Wed–Fri) tell the reader 'this room/day is taken for a longer stretch', so they must stay visually unbroken and clearly wider than a single cell.","groups":["Col 1 (时间段) stands alone: it is the axis every other column is read against, so its widths are set by the time token, not by content length.","Cols 2–6 (周一–周五) are one family of identical role and identical header level; they should be within a few px of each other unless a column's content genuinely demands otherwise, because uneven day widths make horizontal comparison of free slots misleading.","Cols 4–6 (周三/周四/周五) are additionally bound together by the single 全天 banner that spans all three; their combined width is what that one long string has to live in, so they should not be squeezed simultaneously."],"keep_intact":["Time ranges 09:00–10:30, 10:30–12:00, 13:30–15:00, 15:00–16:30, 16:30–18:00 (never split mid-token)","Room codes A301, B202, B105, A301, C20 and 线上","Weekday headers 周一（5/12）… 周五（5/16） on one line","The ｜ separator between event name and room, and the parenthesised times inside event names (keep with their event)","The 3-column banner cell as one unbroken block across 周三–周五"],"may_wrap":["Event titles: 产品需求评审（09:00–12:00）, 供应商准入评审, 研发周会（15:00–16:00）, 周例会（09:30–10:15）, 合同条款会签, 法务咨询, 项目风险同步, 数据看板…, 算法模型…, 新员工入职培训（13:30–16:30）, 客户方案演示与答疑（13:30–16:30）, 产品灰度… — these wrap to 2–3 lines without loss of meaning","The 全天 banner string 2025 春季校园招聘宣讲会（09:00–17:00）｜报告厅 — it has the whole 全天 row to itself, so 2 lines there are free","Wrapping inside the two-row merged blocks (Mon 09:00–12:00, Wed/Thu 13:30–16:30) costs nothing in row height, since those rows are already double height"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [115, 114, 114, 113, 113, 112] · table 682×580px · row heights [60, 60, 106, 106, 60, 106, 83] · column headers wrapped 3/6 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [114, 114, 114, 113, 113, 113] · table 682×580px · row heights [60, 60, 106, 106, 60, 106, 83] · column headers wrapped 3/6 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
